title: Hollywood films and television work
summary: His first film was What's Cooking? around 1940, followed by wartime musicals including Wintertime, independent features and shorts, and later public television.

And when it came time -- near their time to have the baby, the new child, she came home to the folks. And then I came out right about -- actually, before the baby was born, to work out here. We were fortunate enough to arrange it that way. And I did a picture and worked at the Palladium, writing, I guess, and --
What was the picture?
That trip, I'm not sure. The first picture I ever did was called What's Cooking? "?"
What's Cooking? ""
Yeah, with the Andrews Sisters and a bunch of young teenage performers, one of which was Donald O'Connor.
When was that? In the '30s?
Yeah, uh --
Or the '40s?
About 1940.
About 1940.
Yeah, it was Universal. Then we did several movies over a period of years after that.
Uh-huh. What were they?
Oh, typical wartime musicals. Probably the biggest budget picture we did was a Sonya Henning picture "" at 20th Century, called Wintertime.
Oh, yeah.

And a pretty good cast and so on. And then I did a lot of independent pictures. One with Eleanor Powell and W.C. Fields and people like that. And that was with United Artists. And then I did a couple over at Fox, when they figured everybody was making musicals, they'd try it. Actually, I'm speaking of Republic, which was where they made Westerns. But they decided to make musicals, and that was pretty farcical.
This was -- your band was always featured in all these?
Yeah.
Yeah, I think when they have jazz film festivals, they bring out some of those clips.
Yeah. Then we did a lot of shorts for Universal with different people, and things of that nature.
Have you had any special film projects, other than during the years -- I know that for your 40th anniversary there was a great big one.
Well, public television, I've done a lot of that.
Yeah, right.
And a lot of the early stuff with Gleason in San Francisco.
That's right, uh-huh.
And I was still into that sort of thing.
